sentences: In 1891, the foreign secretary haphazardly receives a document from the queen; the document is stolen from his safe later that night.
The famous detective and the doctor discuss the case.

Deciding to lie low for a while, the famous detective informs the doctor that he will delegate cases to his younger brother, the younger detective, who has toiled in his brother's shadow without credit for decades.
At a railway station, the famous detective passes the message to the police headquarters records clerk.
Arriving at the younger detective's flat, the records clerk finds him practicing his fencing and swordplay.
The younger detective expresses bitterness and resentment over being unable to replicate the famous detective's success, mocking his big brother as "a mocking pun on his name".
The younger detective is also a private investigator.

Arriving next is a woman claiming to be a well-known performer, but who is really the singer, a music hall singer who believes she is being blackmailed by the opera singer over a lewd letter she sent him.
The younger detective sees through her immediately.
The younger detective attends one of the singer's performances and twice saves her from attempts on her life.
The next day, he seduces her in her dressing room.
She reveals that she stole the document from the foreign secretary's safe and claims that the foreign secretary is her father.
When the younger detective meets with the foreign secretary, he learns that the singer is in fact the foreign secretary's fiancée.
The opera singer has made a deal with the criminal mastermind to sell him the document, which foreign powers have offered £50,000 to acquire.
The criminal mastermind pays, but the distrustful opera singer proposes that he hand over the document during the debut of his opera so that he has time to deposit the money.
The younger detective and the records clerk infiltrate the opera, which soon devolves into chaos.

The younger detective and the criminal mastermind confront each other backstage and are drawn into a sword fight that corners the younger detective on an outside ledge; the criminal mastermind taunts the younger detective by saying the famous detective was a greater challenge to him because of superior foresight.

Under threat of death, the younger detective agrees to hand over what the criminal mastermind thinks is the document before the chimes of the great clock cause the criminal mastermind to lose balance and plunge into the water below.
The criminal mastermind opens the document to reveal a game of tic-tac-toe: the younger detective had foreseen this and positioned the real document for the famous detective to recover.
The final scene is of the younger detective running through a park to attend the singer and the foreign secretary's wedding.
Sitting on a bench in the park, the singer tells the younger detective that she has called off the wedding, as the famous detective and the doctor watch in disguise.
The younger detective and the singer joyfully reconcile and dance.

The inmate, a convicted thief in a moorland prison, embeds code revealing the hidden location of extremely valuable stolen national bank currency printing plates in the melody notes of three music boxes that he crafts to be sold at auction.
Each box plays a subtly different version of an Australian tune, "a folk song".
At the auction each is purchased by a different buyer.

The doctor's friend, the collector, a music box collector, pays him and the detective a visit and tells them of an attempted burglary in his house the previous night of a plain cheap box (similar to the one he bought at auction) while leaving other much more valuable ones.
The detective asks to see, and he and the doctor are shown the collector's collection.
After they leave, the collector welcomes a female acquaintance, the ringleader, who tries unsuccessfully to buy the auctioned box.
When the collector declines, a male friend of the ringleader's who has sneaked in murders the collector.
At this murder the detective becomes even more curious and learns to whom else the boxes were auctioned off.
The detective and the doctor arrive at the house of the person who bought the second one, just as a strange maid (the ringleader in disguise) is on her way "to go shopping".
The detective later realizes it was not a maid: she locked a child in a closet in order to steal the box from the child.
The detective is able to buy the third box, and upon examination discovers that its variant musical notes' numbers correlate to letters of the alphabet.
The police force fills him in on the stolen bank plates to which the music boxes connect, but all three are needed to decipher the message.
Back at home, their flat is found ransacked, and a cigarette with a distinct type of tobacco is the sole clue.
The detective tracks down the woman who bought the tobacco, the ringleader.
While confronting her, the detective is ambushed by her accomplices, handcuffed, taken to a warehouse, hung by a rafter, and left with poison gas filling the room.
While the detective is narrowly escaping death, the ringleader visits the flat and steals the box from the doctor.
The detective manages to make it back in one piece and, while conversing with him, the doctor offhandedly mentions a quote from the famous writer.
Thinking about this quote, the detective makes a connection as to where the stolen plates may be hidden.

Having stolen all the boxes and deciphered their message, the ringleader and gang join a tour group at the famous writer's house, now a museum, where they slip away and find the plates hidden within a bookshelf.
The ringleader is stealing the plates when the detective ambushes the group.
Police force officers arrest them, and the plates are returned to the bank.
The girl is the youngest child in the detective's family, she is extremely intelligent, observant, and insightful.
Her mother has taught her everything from chess to jujitsu and encouraged her to be strong-willed and independent, to defy the social norms for women of the time.
On her sixteenth birthday, the girl wakes to find that her mother has disappeared, leaving behind only some gifts.
A week later, she meets her older brothers the eldest brother and the detective.

The detective finds her intelligent, whereas the eldest brother finds her troublesome and as her legal guardian, intends to send her away to a finishing school run by the headmistress, his old friend.
The flower cards left by her mother reveal secret messages and lead to hidden money, which the girl uses to escape, disguised as a boy.
On the train, she finds the young viscount hidden in a travel bag.
The girl thinks he is a nincompoop, but warns him that a man in a brown bowler hat, the assassin, is on the train searching for him.
The assassin finds and tries to kill the viscount, who escapes with the girl by jumping off the train.
He forages for edible plants and fungi, they return to the capital and part ways.
Dressed as a Victorian lady, the girl continues to trace her mother, leaving cryptic messages in the newspaper personal advertisements.
The girl discovers pamphlets and a safehouse containing explosives, and learns that her mother is part of a radical group of suffragettes.
She is attacked by the assassin, who interrogates her about the viscount, then attempts to kill her.
The girl fights back, ignites the explosives in the safehouse and escapes.
The girl decides to find the viscount again, to save him from the assassin.
She visits the viscount's family estate, where she meets the viscount's grandmother, the Dowager.
The eldest brother has the inspector of the police headquarters search for the girl.
The girl finds the viscount selling flowers in a market district and warns him of the assassin.
Taking him to her lodgings, she is caught by the inspector, and the eldest brother forces her to go to the headmistress's finishing school.
The detective visits the girl and admits he is impressed by her detective work.
The viscount sneaks into the school and they escape together, stealing the headmistress's motor car.
The girl decides they must go to the viscount's ancestral hall and face the viscount's uncle, who she has deduced was trying to kill him.
The estate is seemingly deserted, but the assassin ambushes them.
The girl trips him using jujitsu, causing a fatal head injury.
The viscount's grandmother is revealed to have hired the assassin.
As a staunch traditionalist, she did not want the viscount to take his father's place in the upper house of parliament and vote for the reform bill.
She shoots him, but he survives, having hidden a plate of armor under his clothes.
The detective arrives at the police headquarters, where the inspector informs him of the girl's actions as they plan to have the Dowager arrested.
The girl shares a tearful goodbye with the viscount.
She eavesdrops on a meeting between the detective and the eldest brother, where the detective suggests becoming her guardian.
Upon returning to her lodgings, the girl finds her mother waiting there.
She explains why she had to leave, and why she must leave again, but she is impressed by what the girl has become.
The girl has found her purpose—she is a detective and a finder of lost souls.
The young detective opens her own detective agency, but is not taken seriously unlike her famous detective brother.
A factory girl asks the young detective to help find her missing sister.
The factory girl takes the young detective to the match factory, which is apparently experiencing a deadly typhus epidemic, and encounters the co-worker, who worked alongside the sisters.
The young detective follows the co-worker to the music hall where the co-worker and the missing sister work as dancers.
She finds a poem written to the missing sister by a secret lover.
On her way home, the young detective comes across the drunken famous detective and brings him home to his lodgings.
He is struggling to solve his latest case involving the blackmail of government officials, but he cannot trace the owner of the accounts where the money is sent.
The young detective deduces that the poem is a code leading to a home in a poor district.
There, she finds the co-worker dying of a stab wound.
The young detective discovers a piece of sheet music in her dress but is interrupted by the superintendent who accuses her of murder.
She escapes to the famous detective's flat and deduces that the missing sister's lover will be at a ball hosted by the factory owner's family.
There, the young detective meets the young lady, a friendly noblewoman, and the secretary, secretary to the treasury minister.
She reunites with the young lord, who teaches her how to dance so she can find an opportunity to get closer to the factory heir, the son of the match factory's owner and the missing sister's lover.
Meanwhile, the famous detective pieces together a message in the blackmail scheme from its mastermind the criminal mastermind.

The young detective is arrested by the superintendent before she can speak with the factory heir, but the famous detective enlists their mother and her fellow radical suffragette to break the young detective out of prison.

While visiting the young lord, the young detective realizes that the missing sister is the young lady and that she, the co-worker, and the factory heir had discovered that white phosphorus, not typhus, was killing the workers, so were planning to expose it.
On the way to the factory, the young detective teaches the young lord how to fight, the two confess their love for each other and share a kiss.
At the factory, they meet the famous detective and find the factory heir dead with a corner of the sheet music.
The three deduce the treasury minister had struck a deal with the factory heir's father to use cheap phosphorus to increase profit.
The group heads to the music hall after realizing the full sheet music was actually a map of the theatre.
There, the missing sister confirms the young detective's findings and admits she and the factory heir needed the young lord's help to expose the treasury minister.
The superintendent and several policemen arrive, holding the factory girl hostage.
However, the factory girl breaks free and a fight ensues, resulting in the young detective defeating the superintendent and causing him to fall to his death.
The treasury minister arrives with the inspector.

He burns the evidence of the dealings and attempts to have the missing sister arrested, but the famous detective and the young detective deduce that the secretary is the criminal mastermind and is responsible for the blackmail and murder.
The secretary is taken into custody.

The missing sister, the factory girl, and the young detective inform the factory's match girls of the events and convince them to strike, the treasury minister is arrested with the young lord's help, and the criminal mastermind escapes police custody.
The young detective sets up a new office at the suffragette's shop.
The young lord has begun courting the young detective in earnest and he invites the young detective to a ball.
The young detective and the young lord have arrived in the island for their wedding.

The ceremony is being held there because the young lord's late father, the old lord, served in the island during the British occupation, and his mother believes it is the most meaningful place for the family.
Her brother attends but is openly against the marriage, believing the young detective is sacrificing her independence to become a Lady.
The young detective insists she can be both a wife and detective.
Meanwhile, her brother is secretly working on another case.
Before he can explain it to the young detective, he disappears.
At the same time, a dying British soldier mutters what sounds like "wrath".
The young detective later deduces he actually said "a name", the surname of the professor.
Searching her brother’s room, the young detective finds a torn piece of an expensive dress.
She tracks the woman through the city, but before she can question her, the woman is shot by a sniper.
As she dies, she warns the young detective "She will kill you".
The young detective pursues the assassin but loses her.
The young detective discovers the "she" is actually the criminal mastermind, who has escaped prison and is living under the alias the professor.
The criminal mastermind has deliberately created the professor identity to manipulate everyone involved.
While the young detective investigates, her brother is revealed to be imprisoned alongside the young lord's mother.

The criminal mastermind explains she arranged almost everything over the previous year, including influencing the young lord's mother into choosing the island for the wedding, because she wanted the young detective to come there.
Her brother's kidnapping is simply bait to lure her into solving a puzzle.
The young detective teams up with the doctor, who has recently entered her brother's life, and a Maltese freedom fighter.
Their investigation uncovers a conspiracy dating back to a battle in the distant country.
During the war, British officers stole a vast quantity of Afghan gold and secretly transported it to the island.
The young lord's father had been involved in transporting the treasure, and his war medals become one of the crucial clues.
The young detective realises a masked man wearing identical medals is actually the brigadier, the young lord's godfather and his father’s closest military friend.
The brigadier, the British governor, and several senior officers all helped cover up the theft of the Afghan gold for decades.
Following her brother’s coded clues, the young detective locates the hidden cave containing the treasure chest.
She knows the criminal mastermind has manipulated her into finding it and expects an ambush.
As soon as she retrieves the chest, the criminal mastermind’s hired Maltese soldiers surround the young detective and the doctor.
In the nick of time, the young lord and the freedom fighter arrive with Maltese rebels, allowing the young detective to escape with the gold.
The criminal mastermind flees on horseback, leading the young detective to the location where her brother and the young lord's mother are being held.
During the fight, the young detective overpowers the criminal mastermind while her brother — after enduring torture — is tempted to kill her.
The young detective persuades him not to become a murderer and together they arrest the criminal mastermind instead.
With the conspiracy exposed, the brigadier confesses his role in stealing the Afghan gold.
He and the other corrupt British officers are arrested and imprisoned.
Rather than allowing the empire to keep the treasure, the young detective and her brother ensure that it is returned to the distant country, acknowledging that it never belonged to the empire.
The freedom fighter believes the scandal will strengthen the island's campaign for independence.
After the case is over, her brother apologises to the young detective for doubting her.
The siblings reconcile, and her brother finally accepts that she has become his equal as a detective.

Deeply disturbed by learning of his father's involvement in British imperial crimes, the young lord renounces his aristocratic title and seat in the upper house of parliament, and chooses to live under his birth name, a plain personal name.
The young detective decides to remain under her own name, keeping her own identity after marriage.
They finally marry in a small clifftop ceremony officiated by her mother.
In 1897 in the capital, a young mouse girl celebrates her birthday with her single father, the toymaker, who is a gifted toymaker.
A bat with a crippled wing and a peg leg arrives and kidnaps the toymaker.
The girl leaves to find the sleuth, the famous great mouse detective.
The surgeon, a retired army surgeon mouse newly returned from a distant country, meets the girl and escorts her to the sleuth's residence.

The sleuth initially dismisses them, but when the girl mentions the bat that abducted her father, the sleuth realizes that the girl saw the bat henchman, the assistant of the professor, the criminal mastermind whom the sleuth was working to catch.

It is then revealed that the professor kidnapped the toymaker to force him to create a clockwork robot replica of the Queen of the Mice, so that the professor can usurp her place as "Supreme Ruler of all the mouse realm".
The toymaker initially refuses to participate in the scheme, but capitulates when the professor threatens to harm the girl.
The bat henchman appears in the sleuth's window, then suddenly disappears.
The sleuth, the surgeon and the girl take the hound, the human detective's pet Basset Hound, to trail the bat henchman's scent.
They trace the bat to a human-sized toyshop.
While searching the area, the surgeon finds the bat henchman's checklist, and the sleuth discovers the bat henchman has been stealing clockwork mechanisms and toy soldiers' uniforms.
The bat henchman ambushes and kidnaps the girl before the sleuth and the surgeon can stop him.
The sleuth conducts chemical tests to the checklist, discovering it came from "the pub", a tavern near the junction of the sewer and the river.
The sleuth and the surgeon disguise themselves as sailors and head to the tavern.
They spot the bat henchman, and follow him to the professor's headquarters, only to be ambushed by the professor and his henchmen.
The professor has the pair tied to a spring-loaded mousetrap connected to an elaborate chain-reaction machine of various killing devices.
The professor then sets out for the royal palace, where his henchmen hijack the royal guards' roles and kidnap the Mouse Queen.
Inspired by a remark the surgeon made, the sleuth deduces the trap's weakness, freeing himself, the surgeon and the girl.
At the royal palace, the professor forces the toymaker to operate the toy Queen, while the real one is taken to be fed to the cat, the professor's pet cat.
The toy Queen declares the professor the ruler of all the mouse realm, and he announces his dictatorial plans for his new "subjects".

After the sleuth, the surgeon, and the girl save the toymaker and the real Queen, they restrain the bat henchman and the professor's other henchmen, while the hound chases the cat until she jumps over a wall, into a pack of Royal Guard Dogs.
The sleuth seizes control of the mechanical queen, making it denounce the professor as a fraud while breaking it into pieces.
Realizing the professor's treason, the enraged crowd attacks, but the professor escapes on his dirigible with the bat henchman, holding the girl hostage.
The sleuth, the surgeon, and the toymaker create an airship from a matchbox, balloons, and a national flag, setting off in pursuit.
The professor tosses the bat henchman overboard to lighten the load.
The sleuth jumps onto the dirigible to confront the professor, causing it to crash straight into the great clock tower's clockface.
Inside the clocktower, the sleuth restrains the professor, rescues the girl, and safely delivers her to the toymaker.
The professor breaks free and attacks the sleuth, just before the clock strikes 10:00; the vibrations cause the professor to fall to his death.
He attempts to take the sleuth with him, but the sleuth grabs a part of the professor's dirigible and saves himself.
Back at the sleuth's residence, the group recounts their adventures.
The toymaker's family bid a fond farewell and leave to catch their train.
The surgeon reluctantly resolves to leave as well, until a new distressed client arrives.
The sleuth introduces the surgeon to her as his friend and investigative partner, prompting the surgeon to remain and assist in the sleuth's future cases.
The detective is viewed as a legendary detective.

Both he and his partner, the doctor, are to view the trial of the professor, but are attacked by a swarm of bees, temporarily waylaid by a package sent by the professor and brought to them by their housekeeper, the landlady.

At the trial, the detective reveals the man accused of the professor's crimes is an imposter, a stand-in, who is incapable of committing the murders due to tremors in his hand caused by excessive masturbation.

Despite attempts by the inspector to convince the detective that his deduction is incorrect, the detective is convinced that the professor is currently traveling to the country overseas while letting the stand-in take the fall for his crimes.

After the trial, the duo travel to the royal palace to attend a surprise birthday party for the detective, where they discover a corpse inside of a birthday cake along with a message from the professor, stating that the queen will die in 3 days' time.
During the autopsy, the detective and the doctor meet the woman physician and the feral woman.
The doctor and the detective become enamored with the woman physician and the feral woman, respectively.
By the end of the autopsy, the doctor declares that the corpse's cause of death is indeterminable, while the detective believes that the person was poisoned.
Furthermore, he believes that the poison came from the poison maker.
The pair eventually locate the poison maker, who is indeed in league with the professor.
Before the poison maker can reveal anything, he is murdered.
The detective decides that he must seek help from his elder brother, who tells him that the murderer is someone close to him.
The detective mistakenly believes the doctor to be the murderer and has him arrested.
He comes to regret this decision, causing his emotions to return.
The detective goes to the doctor's cell, only to find it empty save for a plate filled with red velvet cake crumbs.

Deducing that his housekeeper made the cake and that the doctor left the crumbs to send him a message, he tracks the doctor and the landlady, who is revealed to be the professor's daughter, to the ocean liner, where the murder of the Queen is to take place.
After apologizing to and freeing the doctor, they rush to the main room where they discover a bomb, which the doctor throws out of a window.
The bomb lands in the landlady's boat, killing her and her accomplices.
The pair are congratulated by the Queen, only for the detective to defer the credit to the doctor.
The pair reconnect with the woman physician and the feral woman, the latter of whom reveals that her feral personality was an act to manipulate men.
Each pair shares a kiss before the woman physician and the feral woman head out on the ocean liner.

After returning home, the detective proudly displays a plaque on their building showing that the doctor is a co-detective, finally giving him the recognition he desires (though it is still smaller than the detective's own plaque).
Later, the detective and the doctor confront the professor in a bar in the country overseas.
The film opens with the sudden and mysterious death of the old baronet.
His body is discovered near his family’s ancestral home on the desolate moors of the county, with a look of terror frozen on his face.
Near his body, large paw prints are found, leading many to believe that the legendary family curse—the ghostly hound that haunts the family—has struck again.
The curse is said to stem from a brutal crime committed by an ancestor of the noble family, and the hound has been believed to torment the family for generations.
With the old baronet dead, his heir, the young baronet, returns from a distant country to claim his inheritance.
Concerned for the young baronet’s safety, the family’s friend, the physician, approaches the detective for help.
The physician recounts the legend of the hound and expresses fear that the young baronet might be the next victim.
The detective, intrigued but skeptical about the supernatural element, agrees to take the case.
The detective decides to send the doctor to accompany the young baronet to the ancestral manor while he remains in the capital to continue his investigation in secret.
The doctor’s role is to observe and report back to the detective, while also keeping the young baronet safe.
Upon arriving at the ancestral manor, the doctor notes the gloomy atmosphere of the moors and the imposing estate.
He quickly realizes that there is more to the case than the legend of the hound.
During his stay, the doctor encounters several suspicious characters.
The family servants, the butler and his wife, act strangely, particularly at night.
The doctor notices the butler and his wife signaling someone on the moors using a lantern, which raises his suspicions.
Meanwhile, the doctor meets the local naturalist, a seemingly friendly man who lives nearby with his sister, a young woman.
The young woman, in a moment of fear, secretly warns the young baronet to leave the moors, implying that he is in grave danger.
As the doctor continues his investigation, eerie events unfold.
The terrifying howls of what seem to be a large beast are heard at night across the moors, adding to the belief that the family curse is real.
The doctor tries to piece together the mystery, but without the detective by his side, he feels uncertain about the strange occurrences.
The detective, who has secretly been conducting his own investigation, eventually arrives in the county.
He reveals to the doctor that the mysterious figure on the moors is a fugitive, an escaped convict who has been hiding with the help of the butler and his wife, who are related to him.
However, this discovery is only part of the larger mystery.
The detective uncovers the truth: the legendary hound is not supernatural but a flesh-and-blood dog trained by the naturalist.
It turns out that the naturalist is a distant relative of the noble family, and his goal is to eliminate the young baronet and claim the family estate for himself.
The naturalist has been using the legend of the hound to cover up his murderous plan, taking advantage of the family’s fear of the curse.
In the film’s climax, the detective, the doctor, and the young baronet confront the hound on the moors.
The massive dog, trained to be vicious and appear terrifying, attacks the young baronet.
The detective and the doctor manage to kill the hound before it can fatally wound the young baronet.
In a desperate attempt to escape, the naturalist flees across the great mire, a dangerous and treacherous bog.
Pursued by the detective and the doctor, the naturalist becomes trapped in the mire and sinks to his death.
With the mystery solved, the curse of the family hound is exposed as a fabrication created by the naturalist’s greed and cunning.
The young baronet is saved, and peace is restored to the ancestral manor.
The detective and the doctor return to the capital, having put an end to the dark legacy of the noble family.
For several centuries, the family castle has been haunted by a spooky dog roaming the moor near the stately home.
Its bloodcurdling howl is heard night after night.
The old lord is the latest victim of the ghostly beast.
Lured from the property by a mysterious phone call, he is found dead on the moor, having succumbed to a heart attack from fear.
However, it turns out that the late Lord was not really the last member of the family.
The young lord, a descendant from an obscure branch of the family, unexpectedly arrives to take possession of the castle.
Also staying at the castle is a distant relative of the family, the lady, who originally intended to sell her land and moor to the late Lord.
The young lord quickly falls in love with her.
In order not to let the young lord become another victim of the ghost dog, the executor, a physician, family doctor and friend of the old lord, asks the capital's master detective for help.
As a first measure, the detective sends his faithful companion the doctor to the family castle to keep a close eye on what is happening.
Have the events been orchestrated by the secretive house servant, who has been seen returning light signals coming from the moor at night?
Or is it possible that the escaped convict who went into hiding on the moor, the house servant's brother-in-law, is the mastermind?
And what about the whimsical butterfly collector, a self-confessed nature lover and explorer?
Meanwhile, the detective has travelled to the area incognito and is following a lead.
Telephone calls are made between the family castle and an unknown party at night, and soon the situation becomes more and more threatening for the young lord.
Preoccupied with his new flame, the lady, he does not take the warnings too seriously, which almost costs him his life.
When cries for help ring out from the moor in the middle of the night, the young lord runs there to rescue the woman of his heart who has just been kidnapped.
There he is finally confronted with the ferocious dog.
At the last moment, the detective and the doctor show up and take out the creepy animal with several gunshots.
The butterfly collector, who is behind the attacks, is pursued by the detectives and flees into the depths of the moor, which swallows him up.
The lady, actually the butterfly collector's sister and locked up by him, is freed.
The king of an island kingdom, fearing an imminent assassination attempt, enlists the famous detective to find a body double.
The detective tracks down the double, a notorious debtor from a provincial town, who bears an uncanny resemblance to the king.
Desperate to escape his creditors, the double agrees to the proposal.
Unlike the cowardly king, the young and spirited queen refuses to flee into exile, and the double's bold and energetic approach quickly wins her over.
He impresses her with his fearless participation in bullfights and his calm demeanor during assassination attempts, sparking a passionate affair between the two.
Meanwhile, the treacherous ministers plot to eliminate the double with a bomb concealed in a gramophone, timed to explode during the playing of the new national anthem.
The detective, narrowly escaping a dungeon where the assassins had imprisoned him, saves both the double and the queen just in time.
When the real king dies, the double, who has grown fond of his role as king and fallen for the queen, refuses to relinquish the throne.
Threatening to expose the scandal on an international scale, he forces the ministers to let him remain as king.
